title: Three-manifold surgery presentations and Kirby moves

items.title: Heegaard splitting of a closed oriented three-manifold

references.title: Danny Calegari, Notes on 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Definitions 3.20–3.21, §3, printed pp. 22–23

items.statement:
For $g\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, an **orientable handlebody of genus $g$** is a compact connected orientable smooth $3$-manifold obtained from a $3$-ball by attaching $g$ smooth $1$-handles along orientation-compatible pairs of disjoint boundary disks and rounding the corners. A $1$-handle here is a copy of $D^2\times[-1,1]$ attached by its two end disks to those boundary disks. Its boundary is a connected closed orientable surface of genus $g$. A **Heegaard splitting** of a closed connected oriented smooth $3$-manifold $M$ is a decomposition
$$
M=H_-\cup_{\varphi}H_+
$$
in which $H_-$ and $H_+$ are orientable handlebodies of the same genus, their common boundary is a connected closed surface $\Sigma=\partial H_-=\partial H_+$, and $\varphi:\partial H_-\to\partial H_+$ is an orientation-reversing diffeomorphism whose gluing gives $M$. The surface $\Sigma$ is the **Heegaard surface** of the splitting.

items.title: Dehn twist on an oriented surface

references.title: Robion Kirby, A Calculus for Framed Links in S3
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 36–37; Dehn twists in the Heegaard gluing map

items.statement:
Let $F$ be an oriented smooth surface and let $c:S^1\hookrightarrow F$ be a smooth embedded circle. Choose an annular coordinate map $\phi:S^1\times[-1,1]\to A\subset F$ whose product orientation agrees with the orientation of $F$ and whose core $\phi(S^1\times\{0\})$ is $c(S^1)$. Choose a smooth function $\rho:[-1,1]\to[0,1]$ that is $0$ near $-1$ and $1$ near $1$. The positive **Dehn twist about $c$ in the chosen annular coordinates** is the diffeomorphism that is the identity outside $A$ and on $A$ is
$$
\phi(e^{i\theta},t)\longmapsto\phi(e^{i(\theta+2\pi\rho(t))},t).
$$
The negative Dehn twist is its inverse. The annular coordinates and cutoff are part of the data whenever a representative diffeomorphism is used; its mapping class is its class under smooth isotopy through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $F$.

items.title: Heegaard splitting existence for nonempty closed connected oriented smooth three-manifolds under AC

references.title: Danny Calegari, Notes on 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Proposition 3.22, §3, printed p. 23

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every nonempty closed connected oriented smooth $3$-manifold admits a Heegaard splitting, meaning a union of two orientable handlebodies of the same genus along their common boundary surface.

items.title: A Dehn twist of Heegaard gluing is integral surgery

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Lemma 2.2 and proof, Lecture 2 §2.2, printed pp. 34–35

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M=H_-\cup_\varphi H_+$ be a Heegaard splitting of a closed oriented smooth $3$-manifold, let $\Sigma=\partial H_-=\partial H_+$, and let $c\subset\Sigma$ be an embedded circle with a chosen annular neighbourhood. If $\varphi$ is replaced by $\varphi\circ\tau_c$ or $\varphi\circ\tau_c^{-1}$, where $\tau_c$ is a Dehn twist in the chosen annular coordinates, the resulting oriented $3$-manifold is obtained from $M$ by one surgery on a knot $K$ obtained by pushing $c$ into the interior of $H_-$. The annulus between $c$ and the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of $K$ supplies a framing; the surgery meridian is identified with $\mu+ \lambda_A$ or $\mu-\lambda_A$, according to the twist direction, where $\mu$ is the meridian of $K$ and $\lambda_A$ is the parallel determined by that annulus. Thus the surgery coefficient relative to this framing is integral with absolute value $1$.

items.title: Integral framed-link surgery diagram

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Lecture 2 §2.2, framed links and integral surgery, printed pp. 32–34

references.title: Robion Kirby, A Calculus for Framed Links in S3
references.locator: §1, definition of a framed link and its surgery trace, printed pp. 35–36

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It supplies countable choice for the chosen tubular data: for any sequence of nonempty sets, apply full choice to its range and compose with the index map. Let $L=\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i$ be a finite oriented link in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, where $I$ is a finite index set. For each component $K_i$, choose a closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K_i)$, with the neighbourhoods pairwise disjoint, and include its exterior $E_{K_i}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K_i)$, the positive meridian $\mu_i$, and the preferred longitude $\lambda_i$; the longitude is the degree-one parallel class in $H_1(\partial E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$ that maps to zero in $H_1(E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$. For each $i\in I$, choose an integer $n_i$. The resulting **integral framed-link surgery diagram** is this link and integer family, with the surgery result defined by removing the interiors of all $N(K_i)$ and gluing an oriented solid torus to each boundary torus so that its meridian maps to $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$. If $I=\varnothing$, the surgery result is $S^3$. A diagram is considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying each component framing; a planar projection is only a way of drawing the link.

references.title: Justin Roberts, Kirby calculus in manifolds with boundary

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty closed connected oriented smooth $3$-manifold $M$, there is a finite oriented link $L=\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i\subset S^3$ and an integer $n_i$ for each component such that the oriented manifold obtained by simultaneous surgery with meridian slopes $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$ is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to $M$. The empty link is allowed and presents $S^3$.

items.title: Kirby moves on integral framed links

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Lecture 3 §3.2, Kirby moves K1 and K2, printed pp. 45–46

references.title: Robion Kirby, A Calculus for Framed Links in S3
references.locator: §1, operations (O1) and (O2), printed pp. 35–36

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an integral framed link diagram, **Kirby move equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by the following operations.

1. Apply an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy to the framed link in $S^3$.

2. **Handle slide:** choose distinct components $K_i,K_j$, a parallel $K_j^+$ determined by the framing of $K_j$, and an embedded band whose ends attach to $K_i$ and $K_j^+$ and whose interior misses every link component. Replace $K_i$ by the band sum of $K_i$ with $K_j^+$ and keep the framing obtained by carrying the normal framing across the band. Orient the new component by the band-sum orientation.

3. **Stabilization or destabilization:** add or remove an unknot with framing $+1$ or $-1$ that lies in a $3$-ball disjoint from all the other components.

The integer framing of a component is measured from its preferred longitude as in the integral surgery definition. A planar link projection is not part of the move data; any drawing below is schematic.

items.title: Kirby moves preserve the oriented surgery manifold

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Lecture 3 §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.1 for K1 and K2, printed pp. 46–47

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If two integral framed-link surgery diagrams are related by one ambient isotopy, handle slide, or split $\pm1$-unknot stabilization or destabilization as defined for this page, then their oriented surgery results are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. The same holds for any finite sequence of these moves.

items.title: Zero-meridian pairs are generated by Kirby moves in the three-sphere

references.title: Justin Roberts, Kirby calculus in manifolds with boundary

references.locator: §3.2, framing rule (3.1), printed p. 46; Proposition 3.2 and Figures 3.10–3.12, pp. 47–48; Proposition 3.3 and complete proof, p. 53. The explicit odd/even final deletions are proved below.

references.title: Robion Kirby, A Calculus for Framed Links in S3
references.locator: pp. 35–36, operations and the band-framing formula; p. 53, Remark 4.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a finite integral framed link in the standard oriented $S^3$. In its complement choose an oriented knot $K$ with any integer framing and a small positively oriented meridian $U$ of $K$, with orientation determined by those of $K$ and $S^3$, lying in a ball about one short arc of $K$ and disjoint from $L$. Give $U$ its disk framing zero. Then $L\cup K\cup U$ and $L$ are related by a finite sequence of orientation-preserving ambient isotopies, fully framed handle slides, and insertions or deletions of split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknots. The conclusion applies also to the inverse insertion move. No condition on the knot type of $K$ or on its linking with $L$ is imposed.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D_0$ and $D_1$ be finite integral framed-link surgery diagrams in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, with surgery results $M_0$ and $M_1$. Then $M_0$ and $M_1$ are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic if and only if $D_0$ and $D_1$ are related by a finite sequence of ambient isotopies, framed handle slides, and additions or deletions of split $\pm1$-framed unknots.

title: Three-manifold surgery presentations and Kirby moves — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked cases of three-manifold surgery presentations

references.title: Nikolai Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds
references.locator: Lecture 1 §1.5 and Lecture 2 §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 24–25, 32–37

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The empty integral surgery diagram gives the standard oriented $S^3$. Surgery on the standard unknot with framing $0$ gives $S^1\times S^2$. For every integer $p>0$, surgery on the standard unknot with framing $p$ gives the oriented lens space $L(p,1)$ in the convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

The false claim is that if two integral framed-link surgery diagrams in $S^3$ have orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic surgery results, then the framed links are ambient isotopic.
